result.summary:
Added the F8 p2 block and the {"wasm": id} route target to aegis-config. The acceptance command passes, but merging this commit on its own will stop aegis-bin from compiling (see open issues).

What was built:
- New file crates/aegis-config/src/p2.rs holds the p2 types: P2Block, P2Module, P2Limits, CrashBudget, Isolation and Tenancy.
- Each module's fuel, wall_ms and memory_mib overrides are resolved at load, so every limit has a value and none is optional.
- P2Block::isolation_for applies D1: multi-tenant modules run on p2.isolation (default forkwasm), and single-tenant modules always get a per-principal cordon.
- The route target is now a three-way oneOf: upstream, static or {"wasm": id}.
- Load-time cross-field checks: module ids must be unique (DuplicateModule), and every wasm route must name a declared module (UnknownModule, which also covers a config with no p2 block).
- The effective JSON prints every p2 default, so it round-trips: the reparsed Config is equal and the hash is the same. An absent override and an explicit one equal to the block value hash the same.
- No field can name or share a cordon. The parser accepts only F8's exact member sets (additionalProperties false).
- Files changed: crates/aegis-config/src/{lib.rs,p2.rs,parse.rs,emit.rs}, crates/aegis-config/tests/{p2.rs,store.rs} and the unit JSON.

Tests (new file crates/aegis-config/tests/p2.rs):
- The types are compared with the frozen interfaces/F8-config.schema.json file itself: member sets and order, required lists, integer min/max/default, enums, patterns, and the third oneOf branch.
- Every p2 limit, crash-budget knob and module override is accepted at its minimum and maximum and rejected one past each bound.
- The defaults are checked: 15M fuel, 100 ms, 16 MiB, crash budget 3/60/600, forkwasm for multi-principal modules, mpk false.
- 8 attempts to express a shared cordon are each rejected with UnknownField in 6 places (root, p2, module, crash_budget, route, target).
- About 40 named schema rejects check the error kind and the JSON pointer.

Totality generator (tests/store.rs): added seed E, which uses every p2 member, plus p2 tokens. Each accepted config is checked: wasm routes resolve to a module and all p2 limits are within bounds. The test fails if the generator never reaches p2 on both the accept and reject side.

Results (all on the desktop via ci/remote.sh, so the laptop load average of 12.6 at the time does not affect them; none of these numbers are timings):
- Acceptance command `AEGIS_CONFIG_ITERS=1000000 ci/remote.sh ci/heavy.sh cargo test --release --locked -q -p aegis-config`: exit 0, 451 tests (3 + 100 + 57 + 282 + 9).
- Totality, 1,000,000 inputs: 24,628 accepted (3,442 with a p2 block) and 975,372 rejected (18,742 under /p2 or /to/wasm), across 15 error kinds including UnknownModule.
- `cargo clippy -p aegis-config --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- The debug test run passed as well.

No Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock changes and no new dependencies.
open_issues: Integrator action needed before or with merge: the new RouteTarget::Wasm variant makes the match at crates/aegis-bin/src/plan.rs:228 non-exhaustive. Checked: `cargo check -p aegis-bin` (default and --features native) fails with E0004 `&RouteTarget::Wasm { .. }` not covered. aegis-ops compiles. The fix is a fail-closed arm next to the Static arm: `RouteTarget::Wasm { .. } => return Err(format!("{at}/to: wasm targets are not served by this build (fail closed)")),` until P5-bin-001 wires P2. aegis-bin is outside this unit's write_scope, so the arm was not added here. Without it, gates that build aegis-bin (fail-closed-boot, budget, proxy/native e2e) will not compile on main.

ci/remote.sh does not forward local environment variables, so AEGIS_CONFIG_ITERS=1000000 written in front of `ci/remote.sh` never reaches the remote run. The run still did 1e6 iterations only because the release default is 1,000,000. The totality run with output passed the variable inside the remote command. The gate command has the same issue and works only because of that default.

defaults_json() (`check-config --print-effective` defaults) still prints only canon and limits. P2 defaults appear only in the effective JSON of a config that has a p2 block, and that is where PLAN D7 says p2-e2e reads them. If a standalone p2 defaults dump is wanted, the existing pinned defaults_document test has to change.

result.summary:
Built the aegis-iso P2 sandbox and the p2-subject probe. The acceptance command passes on the laptop (kernel 6.17.0-14-generic, Landlock ABI 7, load average 4.1 to 6.4).

What was built:
- `sandbox::install(&Profile{Zygote|Child|Cordon}) -> Result<Installed, SandboxError>` (crates/aegis-iso/src/sandbox/{mod,filter,landlock,sys}.rs). It runs these steps in order and returns an error at the first one that fails:
  1. Checks the process is single-threaded.
  2. Sets NO_NEW_PRIVS.
  3. Sets RLIMIT_CORE=0 and RLIMIT_NOFILE=256. NPROC is optional for the zygote and cordon; the child always gets NPROC=0.
  4. Sets PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0.
  5. Installs Landlock, or refuses if the ABI is below 4. It handles every filesystem right the ABI knows, allows read only beneath the given paths, handles TCP bind/connect with no rule, and from ABI 6 also scopes signals and abstract UNIX sockets.
  6. Loads the D5 seccomp filter: arch and x32 check; clone3 returns ENOSYS; clone with any CLONE_NEW* flag is killed; a cordon may only clone threads; setsockopt is allowed only at SOL_SOCKET level, so TCP_ULP is killed; prctl options are allowlisted, so PR_SET_DUMPABLE is killed; prlimit64 only on the calling process; an explicit KILL denylist is checked before the allowlist; everything else is killed.
  7. Reads back NO_NEW_PRIVS and dumpable and fails if either is wrong.
- The child profile checks the inherited sandbox, then stacks a filter that kills clone, fork, vfork, execve and execveat.
- aegis-iso has 8 of its 20 allowed unsafe sites, all in sys.rs plus one in the probe, each with a `// SAFETY:` comment.
- The probe protocol from oracles/syscall-negative/README.md is in sandbox/probe.rs behind `test-hooks`. It writes installed, armed, result and child-exit JSON lines. `p2-subject probe` drives it; `p2-subject serve` exits 78 until P5-iso-002/003 add it.

Gate results:
- `oracles/syscall-negative/run --subject 'target/p2/release/p2-subject probe'`: PASS, 77/77 cells on 3 stages, 5 masked controls. Every kill probe died with SIGSYS and clone3 returned ENOSYS at the cordon, zygote and fork-child stages. PR_GET_DUMPABLE read 0 in all three. open_outside got EACCES from Landlock. connect_tcp died with SIGSYS because connect is on the seccomp denylist.
- `--self-test`: PASS, 7/7 mutants red, reference green on 77 cells.
- `cargo xtask unsafe-sites`: PASS (aegis-iso 8/20, aegis-wasm 0/1); its self-test also passes.
- `cargo xtask layering`: PASS.
- clippy `-D warnings`: clean on aegis-iso and p2-subject, with and without test-hooks.
- `cargo test -p aegis-iso`: 14/14. This includes a classic-BPF interpreter test of the filter layout and two tests that install refuses before changing anything.

Extra check, not committed: I built two weakened versions of the real subject. With the child filter skipped, the gate failed on forkwasm-child:fork (errno 11; NPROC=0 still stopped the fork, but without SIGSYS). With Landlock skipped, it failed on open_outside at all 3 stages.

Landlock ABI 7 is recorded in the oracle's host facts and in the subject's installed line.
open_issues: Cargo.lock: --locked needs a new path-only p2-subject entry (7 lines, no third-party change). I generated it locally to run the acceptance and did not commit it; the integrator must re-lock at merge.

Feature unification: p2-subject turns on aegis-iso/test-hooks (it needs the probe, and p2-subject cannot contain unsafe code). Cargo merges features across packages built in one command, so P5-iso-002/003's `cargo build -p p2-subject -p aegis-p2` into target/p2 would compile aegis-iso with test-hooks inside the shipped aegis-p2 build. test-hooks only adds the probe module and never changes install(), but this conflicts with D15's rule that target/p2 holds only the shipped configuration. Suggested fix: build p2-subject and aegis-p2 in separate commands or separate target dirs, or have the integrator decide.

RLIMIT_NPROC: zygote and cordon profiles leave NPROC unset by default (Profile.nproc = None). NPROC counts every process of the real uid, so a small value breaks fork and threads on a shared-uid host such as the laptop. The fork child always gets NPROC=0. A real per-worker NPROC needs a dedicated worker uid; that is for P5-iso-002/003 or the integrator.

Not yet tested against Wasmtime: the seccomp allowlist was written for Rust std, glibc, the Wasmtime runtime and fd-passing I/O, but only the probe has run under it. P5-iso-002/003 may need to add syscalls when the real zygote and cordon run. The denylist is checked before the allowlist, so an addition there cannot re-allow a denied call.

Choices that go further than the reference probe: connect, bind and listen are killed by seccomp (the reference allows connect so Landlock's net rule is what the probe sees). As a result the connect_tcp probe shows SIGSYS, and the Landlock TCP rule, although installed, is not exercised by the gate. kill and ioctl are also killed.
Not run at this wave: the gate's aegis-p2 half (`target/p2-test/release/aegis-p2 probe`), which P5-iso-002/003 run; and kamrui or desktop runs, which belong to P5-vps-001.

result.summary:
Built the aegis-wasm runtime and the aegis-p2 `config` / `compile` subcommands. One caveat: the binary only runs `config --json` once main.rs is wired, and main.rs is outside my write scope (see open issues).

What was built (worktree /home/patrickd/aegis/.claude/worktrees/wf_08057dd3-98e-4):
- crates/aegis-wasm/src/engine/mod.rs: `EngineSettings` is the one value the wasmtime Config is built from. It fixes the security settings: pooling allocator, 4 GiB reservation, 32 MiB guard (also placed before the memory), signal-based traps, memory64 and gc off, threads and component model reported false (their features are absent), epoch and fuel on, MPK only Yes or No. From F8 it takes only `memory_mib`, `cordon_slots` and `mpk`. `P2Engine` keeps the settings it was built from, and `config --json` prints `engine.settings().to_json()`, not a separate literal. Also here: bounded `P2Limits` that refuse out-of-range values instead of clamping, and an `EpochTicker` that counts real elapsed time, so oversleeping does not add up. The epoch deadline is set a tenth under wall_ms.
- crates/aegis-wasm/src/engine/cwasm.rs: `compile` checks the module against the engine and the F14 shape. `load` reads the file once, checks its sha256 against the expected digest and refuses on a mismatch. It then checks the bytes are a precompiled module, and only then deserializes. This is the crate's only unsafe site, with a `// SAFETY:` comment.
- crates/aegis-wasm/src/store/mod.rs: `Worker` holds the engine and a pre-resolved module. Every request gets a fresh Store, a memory limiter at memory_mib (tables capped at 10,000 elements, one instance per Store), and fuel and the epoch deadline set before instantiation. Traps map to the F14 codes; handle() 0 is Allow, 1 is Deny, anything else is Error.
- crates/aegis-wasm/src/abi/mod.rs: F14 import allowlist and export shape only. `define_imports` defines nothing, so a module that imports a host function fails to link (fail closed until P5-wasm-002).
- crates/aegis-p2/src/config.rs: `dispatch()` handles `config --json [--mpk]` and `compile --in --out [--mpk] [--memory-mib] [--pool-slots]`. `compile` refuses to run unless /proc/self/status shows NoNewPrivs 1 and Seccomp 2, and writes the .cwasm as 0600 through a temp file and rename.
- crates/aegis-wasm/tests/engine.rs: 10 tests with hand-encoded Wasm guests.

Gate results:
- Release build of aegis-p2 into target/p2 (local, under heavy.sh): OK, 2m14s.
- `ci/wasmtime-config.py check --worker target/p2/release/aegis-p2`: PASS (pin 50.0.1, 9 features exact, 1 deserialize site, static and runtime halves). This ran with the temporary main.rs wiring described in open issues.
- `ci/wasmtime-config.py --self-test`: PASS, clean fixture green and 25/25 mutants red.
- `ci/remote.sh ci/heavy.sh cargo test --locked -q -p aegis-wasm`: 10/10 on the desktop (load 1.10). Also 10/10 on the laptop (load 6.59), where the MPK engine is actually built and run.
- `cargo xtask unsafe-sites`: PASS (aegis-wasm 1/1, aegis-iso 0/20); its self-test rejects 7/7 mutants. Clippy with `-D warnings` on aegis-wasm and aegis-p2 (all targets) is clean.

The tests cover each item in acceptance.must:
- Fresh Store per request: the poison guest answers correctly for 200 requests in a row, and a poison-then-trap guest traps the same way 50 times. A control shows that one reused instance does return the poisoned answer (0 then 1).
- Fuel: 15M fuel stops a loop with an out-of-fuel trap after 12.7 ms on the desktop (load 1.10) and 5.8 ms on the laptop (load 6.59).
- Epoch: a loop given fuel 1e9 traps on the wall bound within wall_ms. Desktop, older margin (load 1.10): 18.1 ms for 20, 49.6 for 50, 99.6 for 100. Laptop, current margin (load 6.59): 17.4, 45.6, 89.9.
- Limiter: growing to exactly 16 MiB or 4 MiB succeeds and one page more returns -1. The 4 MiB case is below the 16 MiB pool slot, so the limiter is what refuses. A 100-page initial memory under 4 MiB fails as a memory trap.
- Wrong digest: a flipped digest, a tampered file, and garbage with a wrong digest are all refused as DigestMismatch. Garbage or plain .wasm with a matching digest is refused as not a precompiled module, also before deserialize.

Timing numbers are provisional, with load average recorded next to each.
open_issues: Runtime half needs main.rs wiring that I could not commit: crates/aegis-p2/src/main.rs is owned by P5-iso-002. The runtime PASS above was produced with this applied temporarily and then reverted: add `mod config;` and, at the start of main(), `let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect(); if let Some(code) = config::dispatch(&args) { return code; }`. On commit 67903f3 alone, `aegis-p2 config --json` still exits 78, so the wasmtime-config runtime half stays red until P5-iso-002 or the integrator adds those lines.

Deviation from the literal acceptance.must: the unsafe site is `Module::deserialize(engine, &bytes)` over the exact in-memory bytes that were hashed, not `Module::deserialize_file`. deserialize_file reopens and maps the path after the check, leaving a window to swap the file. The oracle and xtask accept it (1 site, under crates/aegis-wasm/src/). The cost is an anonymous copy of the module in zygote RSS instead of file-backed pages. Integrator to confirm.

MPK on the AMD desktop: wasmtime 50 enables MPK only on Intel x86_64 (CPUID vendor check), even though the desktop reports pku. A `--mpk` Engine cannot be built there, and a worker with p2.mpk = true would refuse to boot (Yes never falls back to off; a test asserts this). So that the wasmtime-config gate can run on the desktop, `config --json --mpk` on such a host builds the wasmtime Config, skips the Engine, prints a note to stderr and prints the settings. On the laptop and kamrui (Intel) the MPK Engine really is built. PLAN D11 says 'all three hosts report pku', but in wasmtime's terms MPK is usable on 2 of 3.

The `compile` sandbox is not installed by aegis-p2 yet: aegis-iso is still a stub (P5-iso-001 runs in parallel). As a backstop, `compile` refuses unless NoNewPrivs=1 and Seccomp=2. P5-iso-002 must install the cordon profile without network (Landlock: read --in, write the --out directory) before calling config::dispatch. The compile CLI was never run end to end inside a real sandbox; the library compile and load path is tested.

abi::check_module enforces F14 'exports exactly memory and handle' at compile. Toolchain-built guests that also export __heap_base or __data_end will be refused. That matches F14 as written; P5-wasm-002 and the hostile/e2e oracles should expect it.

Fuel calibration: a tight `loop br 0` uses 15M fuel in 12.7 ms on the desktop and 5.8 ms on the laptop, slower than the q4-006 figure of about 2 ms, which was measured on a different guest. Recorded only; D6 makes fuel accounting, and the wall bound is the DoS bound.

The epoch deadline is wall_ms minus max(1 tick, 10%), at 1 ms ticks, so a 100 ms wall bound traps at about 90 ms. That was chosen so the trap stays within wall_ms under load. P5-iso-002/003 should confirm it suits the cordon path (the fork child uses ITIMER_REAL instead).
